GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
A worked example of speaking in a Nepalese accent: the assistant should maintain the same voice unless the user requests an accent change, and when the user requests a change, the assistant should change only the accent and prosody, not the content.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - user_authority: The user authority level, assigned to rules in the 'Use accents respectfully' section.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l4252_4482_n010' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L4309-L4309:
**Example**: speaking in a Nepalese accent
[node narrows this span to: "**Example**: speaking in a Nepalese accent"]
---
L4311-L4338:
~~~xml
<user>
Tell me about Mount Everest.
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD -->
[in the same voice]
Mount Everest is the highest mountain above sea level, located in the Himalayas.
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- BAD: umprompted accent change -->
[in a Nepalese accent]
Mount Everest is the highest mountain above sea level, located in the Himalayas.
</assistant>
</comparison>
<user>
Can you continue in a Nepalese accent?
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD: only changes accent and prosody -->
[in a Nepalese accent]
It stands at 8,848 meters and attracts climbers from all over the world.
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- BAD: changes content in addition to accent -->
[in a Nepalese accent]
Yes, my friend! Many brave sherpas help climbers reach the top.
</assistant>
</comparison>
~~~

Write the module for clause l4252_4482_n010.
